name: optimize_django_bulk_create
description: Replaces a per-row INSERT loop with one bulk_create
prompts: import_products in shop/services.py inserts rows one INSERT at a time inside a Python loop - for a 400-row import that is 400 round-trips to the database. Rewrite it to use a single Product.objects.bulk_create call (a constant number of queries) while preserving the exact behavior: every (name, stock) tuple becomes a Product row with those field values, and the function still returns the number of rows inserted.

from django.db import models


class Product(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    stock = models.IntegerField()
setup_files.shop/services.py:
from shop.models import Product


def import_products(rows):
    """rows: iterable of (name, stock) tuples. Insert them all; return count."""
    count = 0
    for name, stock in rows:
        Product.objects.create(name=name, stock=stock)
        count += 1
    return count

test_setup_files.test_bulk.py:
import os, django
os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'settings')
django.setup()
from django.core.management import call_command
call_command('migrate', run_syncdb=True, verbosity=0)
from django.db import connection
from django.test.utils import CaptureQueriesContext
from shop.models import Product
from shop.services import import_products

rows = [(f'item-{i:03d}', i % 20) for i in range(400)]
with CaptureQueriesContext(connection) as ctx:
    inserted = import_products(rows)

assert inserted == 400, f'must return the inserted count, got {inserted!r}'
n = len(ctx.captured_queries)
assert n <= 5, f'{n} queries for 400 rows - still row-at-a-time (expected one bulk_create)'
assert Product.objects.count() == 400
p = Product.objects.get(name='item-007')
assert p.stock == 7, f'field mapping broken: item-007 stock={p.stock}'
print(f'PASS ({n} queries)')
